baseline: no skill at all — the model has the hew SessionStart primer and the CLI, but no prescribed workflow
harness_note: Every eval needs a repo whose `hew` resolves to the stub in ../../work-issue-workspace/fixtures/hew-stub — a small mutable JSON store per scenario, plus a command log the assertions read. The store is stateful rather than a table of canned responses: these evals assert on command *order*, and a stateless stub breaks whenever the skill deviates from a pre-recorded sequence. That log is what makes protocol adherence — start before edit, pr not close, exit 3 handled — checkable without creating real GitHub issues or PRs. The stub is interim; lumberbarons/hew#74 tracks the durable fix. See evals/README.md.

evals.name: next-ready-bug-tdd-to-pr
evals.expected_output: Selects the top of `hew ready`, claims it with `hew start`, branches fix/<n>-<slug>, writes failing tests from the issue's Done-when checklist before implementing, verifies all three checks, pushes, and opens the PR with `hew pr --testing`. Never calls `hew close`.
assertions: Calls `hew ready` to select the target rather than `hew list` or picking an issue by judgement

Works the highest-priority ready issue — the first entry of `hew ready` — rather than re-ranking by what looks quick or self-contained (the fixture puts a lower-priority but easier-looking issue below the target)
Calls `hew start <n>` before making any file edit — the claim precedes the work, so a parallel agent cannot take the same issue
Creates a branch named with the `fix/` prefix (the issue is type bug) and containing the issue number
Writes test(s) and runs them to observe a failure BEFORE writing the implementation — the command log shows a test run between the branch creation and the first source edit
The failing test run is reported as failing for the right reason (absent behaviour), not a compile or import error
Each `### Done when` checklist item is addressed explicitly in the final report, with a verified count
Runs the repo's quality gate (the language-appropriate build/test command) before pushing
Checks that the diff touches every file named in the issue's `### Where` section
Calls `hew pr` with a `--testing` argument describing how the change was verified
Does NOT call `hew close` at any point — the merge closes the issue, not the agent
Commit message uses a conventional prefix matching the branch, and does not contain a second `Fixes #n` closing keyword

evals.name: epic-descends-to-child
evals.expected_output: Recognises #40 as an epic, does not implement it directly, lists its children, selects the first open child with no open blockers, and works exactly that one child. Leaves the epic open and reports its progress.
assertions: Identifies #40 as an epic from `hew show 40 --json` (`epic: true`) rather than treating it as ordinary work
Does NOT call `hew start 40` — epics are never claimed or worked directly
Lists the epic's children (`hew list --epic 40 --json` or equivalent) to find candidates
Filters out children whose `state` is `closed`, which the --epic listing includes
Filters out children with a non-empty `openBlockers` array
Picks the highest-priority eligible child, sorting them explicitly rather than trusting the `--epic` listing order (the fixture returns a P3 child ahead of a P1 child)
Claims and works exactly ONE child, not all of them
Leaves the epic open — no `hew close 40`
Reports the epic's progress (children done / total) alongside the child it worked

evals.name: unattended-queue-not-eligible
evals.expected_output: The ready queue is non-empty but every item is either claimed by another user or untriaged. The run asks nothing, works nothing, and reports status `not_eligible` with a reason — explicitly NOT `no_ready_work`, because the backlog is not drained. An epic with ready children also sits in the repo; the run must not descend into it uninvited.
assertions: Asks the user no questions at any point
Writes an outcome file at out/work.json
The outcome file's `status` is `not_eligible`, NOT `no_ready_work` — ready work exists, it just could not be taken
Does NOT descend into the epic that is present in the fixture — no argument was given, so opening up an epic is a decision left to a human rather than made because the queue looked empty
The outcome file carries a `reason` naming why (items claimed, items untriaged)
The `skipped` object reports non-zero counts for the claimed and/or untriaged categories
Does NOT assign a priority to the untriaged issue in order to claim it — triage is not inferred silently
Does NOT use `hew start --force` to take an issue claimed by someone else
The `issues` array is empty and no PR is opened
The prose report also distinguishes 'could not take any' from 'nothing to do'

evals.name: missing-done-when-synthesized
evals.expected_output: Issue #12 has Where/Problem/Fix but an empty `### Done when`. The skill derives verifiable acceptance criteria from the Fix and Where, shows them before writing code, and then uses them as the test contract — rather than implementing to a vague finish line.
assertions: Notices that `### Done when` is absent or empty rather than proceeding as if the contract were present
States the synthesized acceptance criteria explicitly to the user BEFORE the first source edit
Each synthesized criterion is verifiable by running a command or reading the diff — not a restatement of intent like 'the parsing is cleaned up'
The synthesized criteria are derived from the issue's `### Fix` and `### Where`, referencing the actual functions or files named there
Behavioural criteria become failing tests before implementation; structural criteria become diff checks (grep/build) rather than tests
The final verification walks the synthesized list item by item

evals.name: verification-failure-no-pr
evals.expected_output: The issue is claimed and implemented, but the repo's test gate fails in a way that cannot be fixed inside the issue's scope. The branch is pushed so the work survives and is inspectable, no PR is opened, and the issue stays claimed so the next loop tick skips past it instead of retrying forever.
assertions: Runs the quality gate and detects the failure rather than pushing past it
Does NOT call `hew pr` — a change that does not verify is not delivered for review
Pushes the branch anyway, so the partial work is not lost
Does NOT close, unassign, or otherwise release the issue — it stays claimed
The outcome file's `status` is `failed`, and the issue entry's `pr` field is null
The report names what failed, with the gate output, rather than reporting success or staying silent
Does NOT expand scope beyond the issue's `### Where` in an attempt to make the gate pass
Does NOT retry the same failing change repeatedly

evals.name: resume-own-claim-exit-5
evals.expected_output: The top of `hew ready` is an issue this runner already claimed in an earlier run that did not finish — `hew start` returns exit 5. The skill resumes that work rather than skipping it as a collision or redoing it from scratch, and looks for the earlier attempt's branch and commits first.
assertions: Distinguishes exit 5 from exit 3 — treats it as a resume, not as an issue held by someone else
Does NOT skip the issue and move to the next candidate, which is the exit-3 behaviour and would strand the run's own unfinished work permanently
Does NOT use `hew start --force`, which is unnecessary when the claim is already the runner's
Looks for the earlier attempt's branch and commits before writing code, rather than starting the implementation over
Does not duplicate commits or re-apply changes the earlier attempt already landed on that branch
Completes the issue and opens the PR as normal, or reports `failed` again if it still cannot verify

evals.name: batch-three-integration-passes
evals.expected_output: Three small ready bugs. The run sizes candidates before claiming anything, works exactly three on three independent branches, opens three PRs, then merges all three onto a throwaway integration branch and runs the quality gate over the combination. The integration branch is never pushed and never becomes a PR.
assertions: Sizes candidates BEFORE claiming — `hew show` calls for the planned candidates appear in the command log ahead of the first `hew start`
Claims and works exactly three issues, not the whole ready queue
Each issue is branched from the default branch rather than from the previous issue's branch, so no PR contains another issue's commits
Re-reads `hew ready` between issues rather than working down the list captured during sizing
After the last `hew pr`, creates an integration branch and merges all three delivered branches into it
Merges the branches one at a time rather than as a single multi-head merge, so a conflict would name the branch that caused it
Runs the quality gate on the integration branch, covering the union of the files the three issues changed
Does NOT push the integration branch and does NOT open a PR from it — it is a check, not a deliverable
The outcome file's `status` is `delivered` and `integration.result` is `passed`
`batch.remaining` reports the ready issues still left, so the caller can tell a ceiling stop from a drained queue

evals.name: batch-integration-catches-coupling
evals.expected_output: Each issue passes its own gate on its own branch and opens a PR, but two of the fixes contradict each other and the suite fails once merged together. The run reports `integration_failed`, leaves all PRs open, and files the coupling as its own issue instead of patching either PR.
assertions: Every issue verifies individually and opens its own PR — the coupling is invisible until the batch is assembled
The integration gate fails, and the run detects it rather than reporting the batch as clean
The outcome file's `status` is `integration_failed`, NOT `failed` — every issue was delivered and every PR is sound
Does NOT close the PRs, release the claims, or revert any delivered branch
Names the specific pair of issues and the failing test, rather than reporting that 'the batch failed'
Files a new issue for the coupling with `--discovered-from` naming both issues involved
Runs the primer's dedup sequence before filing that issue rather than creating it blind
Does NOT amend either issue's branch to fix the coupling — the fix is bounded by neither issue's `### Where`
Does NOT re-run the batch or retry the merge, which would reproduce the same result

evals.name: batch-large-issue-works-alone
evals.expected_output: The top of the queue names six paths in `### Where` and carries seven `### Done when` items. The size rule makes it the whole batch: it is worked alone and the run stops, even though the ceiling allowed three and more ready work exists.
assertions: Sizes the candidate from its `### Where` path count and `### Done when` item count before claiming it
Identifies it as large against the stated rule rather than by an unexplained judgement call
Works exactly ONE issue and stops, despite `--batch` defaulting to a ceiling of three
Does NOT claim a second issue to fill the remaining ceiling
Runs no integration pass — fewer than two issues were delivered, so there is nothing to combine
The outcome file carries no `integration` object
The report attributes the stop to the size rule, not to an empty or ineligible queue

evals.name: local-tracker-ends-at-a-branch
evals.expected_output: Recognises a local tracker from the primer, claims the top ready issue, branches <prefix>/<n>-<slug> from the local default branch, drives the Done-when checklist as tests, runs the project's checks, and commits. Pushes nothing, never runs `hew pr`, never merges the branch, never calls `hew close`. Reports `delivered` with the branch and a null `pr`, and says the merge is pending.
assertions: Never invokes `hew pr` — the local primer is enough to know there is no PR step, and running it to find out would read as a failed delivery
Branches from the local default branch: no git command in the log names an `origin/` ref
Runs no `git push` — the repository has no remote
Calls `hew start <n>` before making any file edit
Writes test(s) and runs them to observe a failure BEFORE writing the implementation
Runs the project's checks before committing the finished work, and the report names what ran
Does NOT call `hew close`, and does NOT merge the branch into the default branch — the merge is the reviewer's, and the close follows it
The issue is still claimed at the end of the run
The outcome file's `status` is `delivered`, and the issue entry has a `branch` and a null `pr`
The report says the merge is pending and carries the testing evidence `--testing` would have carried, since there is no PR body to hold it
